description:
You are an Environmental Restoration Planner assessing the computational mesh of a HEC-RAS 2D hydraulic model of the White River through Muncie, Indiana. Before running new restoration scenarios, you need to document the existing mesh properties.

The plan HDF file is located at:
  /home/ga/Documents/hec_ras_projects/Muncie/Muncie.p04.tmp.hdf

Using Python with h5py and numpy, explore the HDF5 file structure to find the 2D flow area geometry data (typically under /Geometry/2D Flow Areas/). Then extract and analyze the computational mesh properties.

Produce TWO output files:

1. A text report at /home/ga/Documents/hec_ras_results/mesh_analysis_report.txt containing:
   - Total number of 2D computational cells across all flow areas
   - Number of 2D flow areas and their names
   - For each 2D flow area:
     * Cell count
     * Minimum cell elevation (from 'Cells Minimum Elevation' dataset)
     * Maximum cell elevation
     * Mean cell elevation
     * Standard deviation of cell elevations
     * Spatial extents: min X, max X, min Y, max Y (from 'Cells Center Coordinate' dataset)
     * Domain width (max X - min X) and domain height (max Y - min Y)

2. A CSV file at /home/ga/Documents/hec_ras_results/mesh_cell_data.csv with columns:
   area_name, cell_index, center_x, center_y, min_elevation
   (one row per computational cell)

The HDF file should already exist from a previous simulation run. Use h5py to navigate the HDF5 hierarchy and extract the relevant datasets. Look for datasets named 'Cells Center Coordinate' (Nx2 array of X,Y) and 'Cells Minimum Elevation' (N array) within each 2D flow area group.
